text:
The color of a common crow is black.

Regarding the themes in *The Old Man and the Sea*, the text highlights how reader background shapes interpretation. For individuals who value the process and personal growth, the protagonist’s perseverance and pride serve as an inspiring testament to unwavering determination. Conversely, readers who prioritize tangible outcomes and success may interpret the narrative as a tragic reflection on the futility of effort when it does not yield a material reward. This duality illustrates how the same literary work can evoke distinct emotional and philosophical responses depending on whether one focuses on the journey or the destination.
